problem_desc:
Background: Currently; ARL S8161 BGA is using multiple zone and heater current is ~370W much higher than the chiller capacity recommended value 266W; it should be high risk to cause chiller overstress when load to 30cells (learning from MTLH6). During investigation on heater current issue; the team detected that there is no matching between AP pedestal design with physical unit. Follow design rule; zone 0 should be match with CPU and zone1 should be match with PCH. However; the current design is zone0 control PCH and zone1 control CPU. This is the main root cause which caused heater power increase. The solution is changing configuration from Multiple zone to Single zone (Change TCC switch position from '7' to '5'). Therefore; the PWP for Heater current reduction by converting from Multizone to Single Zone must encompass all necessary changes to meet requirements for heater power reduction on ARL S8161 BGA. The xRB team is coordinating with the open DRB #12321349 documentation to begin data collection on ARL S8161 BGA once volume is available under the approved PWP 2024.44.AT Integrated CCB.18.PWP

problem_desc: Starting from WW02.6N; we observed high OOC triggers on CMP-H PCH (V8) on top 03 alarm code MV8BXX (bin 46xx); MV8B15 (bin 15xx); and MV8B11 (bin 11xx) which brought up alarm rate x4-5 times in subsequent shifts. problem_desc:
Currently; EHB products have high PyPCS trigger MI02/MI03 loss code that impacted to EUPH/Operation workload. As the historical data show; PyPCS triggered with some sub apps on EHB to detect MI02/MI03 signal; but the defects were not met IRVI reject criteria. All cases have no strong CA and no abnormal findings on HDMx hardware. After reviewing with ADVI ME confirmed that these signals were over triggers and cannot optimize ADVI's module recipe as might cause other defects to escape. Besides; MI02/MI03 hard reject also has PyPCS implement (using IRVI data for running CA and trigger); so there is a low risk for the escapee. After releasing new limit PyPCS on EHB for 4 specific sup-app (SI-DIE-T-BODY1; SI-SUB-T-BODY5; SI-DIE-T-BODY3; SI-DIE-T-RSDFU2) in WW37’22; team review number of triggers with new limit loosen and observed that number of invalid triggers were reduced and all triggers do not meet IRVI reject criteria and pass 100%. HDMx team will collect more data and go with FWP submission.

 

PyPCS trigger rate

         

Failure rate

  1. SI-DIE-T-BODY1: epoxy haze causing invalid trigger at HDMx => checked and confirmed with DVI engr => can’t optimize by DVI recipe => loosen limit at the specific area (X<725) of PCH die with failure rate limit 0.2; that will reduce ~95% invalid trigger

 

 

  1. SI-DIE-T-BODY2 & SI-DIE-T-RSDFU2: Stain at Edge CPU Die => valid trigger at HDMx due to HW limitation (Actual Pan cannot remove completely LTIM stain at the edge of die (at the pedestal chamfer) and cannot optimize on module recipe too). Besides that; the defects were not met IRVI reject criteria => loosen with limit as below:
  • SI-DIE-T-BODY2: at X<1150 of CPU die with a failure rate limit of 0.3 => reduce ~94% invalid trigger
  • SI-DIE-T-RSDFU2: at X<1170 & Y>1050 of CPU die with a failure rate limit of 0.2 => reduce ~95% invalid trigger

            A1:   Open DRB to collect data for module recipe optimization of product ARL S8161 BGA?

Q2: Why need to optimize module recipe of product ARL S8161 BGA?

            A2: To resolve the high heater power issue on ARL S8161 BGA?
problem_desc: Currently; ARL S8161 BGA is using multiple zone and heater current is ~370W much higher than the chiller capacity recommended value 266W; it should be high risk to cause chiller overstress when load to 30cells (learning from MTLH6) Short term; Run with < 22 cell/tool (potential impact 26% to capacity loss) and mixing with products low power. During investigation on heater current issue; team detected that there is no matching between AP pedestal design with physical unit. Follow design rule; zone 0 should be match with CPU and zone1 should be match with PCH. However; the current design is zone0 control PCH and zone1 control CPU. This is the main root cause which caused heater power increase. The solution is changing configuration from Multiple zone to Single zone (Change TCC switch position from '7' to '5'). Therefore; the PWP for Heater current reduction by converting from Multizone to Single Zone must encompass all necessary changes to meet requirements for heater power reduction on ARL S8161 BGA. The xRB team is coordinating with the open DRB # documentation to begin data collection on ARL S8161 BGA once volume is available under the approved PWP 2024.44.AT Integrated CCB.18.PWP

Occurred root cause: The root cause of the issue is the presence of 3 bad cells (LTIM valves) and 6 bad APs (heaters); which led to a significant increase in bin 97 occurrences. Combined with an ineffective bin 97 PCS trigger; this resulted in massive yield loss for bin 97. 

5-Whys

  1. Why do we need to open DRB?

    Because lot U507G220_7820 is showing a high B97 yield loss when run on HXV026 (~8.5% compared to the baseline of 3%).
  2. Why is lot U507G220_7820 showing high B97 yield loss on HXV026?

  4. Additionally; the ineffective bin 97 PCS trigger contributed to the significant yield loss.

  5. Why did bad cells induce B97?
    Because marginal LTIM valves led to low LTIM pressure and insufficient LTIM amounts during dispense/insitu-dispense and poor thermal contact.
  6. Why did bad APs induce B97?
    Due to degraded pedestals causing inefficient thermal control; which resulted in bin 97.
  7. Why did pedestals induce B97?
    Because the heater inside pedestal; a run-to-fail part responsible for temperature control and heating; eventually fails. This leads to inefficient thermal transfer and results in bin 97 issues.

Executive Summary: The ADLN product has high PyPCS trigger MI04 loss code that impacted to EUPH/Operation workload. root_cause_desc:
Exact Root Cause is unknown due to lack of evidence / tool logs not verbose enough 

Contributing Causes:

Fishbone chart

Primary Cause: Tool assigned wrong VID to 2 units  

1 – Why 1u untested escaped all the way to TTT and not rejected by Finish? 

=>   Finish modules like LM and DVI only check latest ULT status of units. In the case of PPV untested; latest ULT status will be Good from upstream (Class Test).      

2 – Why was it not rejected by wrong ULT linkage at PPV? 

=> Miscommunication during lot-on-hold dispo led to lot moved out before all 3 impacted units demix; and the SC allowed MoveOut qty > ULT good qty.     

3 – Why Untested unit escaped into Pass bundle at PPV? 

=> In 1A; unit VID was wrongly assigned to another unit. It tested Pass due to TP has no FuseCheck; instead relying on ULT system and LoH process to reject units with wrong VIDóEfuse linkage. In 1C; unit was scanned correctly and marked as Pass based on 1A data (with wrong VID). 

4 – Why tool did not alarm if VID scanned wrong? 

=> Tool only alarm if scanned a duplicated VID. In the problem scans sequence; the 1st scan was a no-read; so there was no duplicated VID to detect. 

5 – Why Vision scan result still wrong?

=> Unknown. Suspect comms problem between Handler and Camera causing Vision to receive VID of the previous scan after a no-read.

 

See attached STH095_X207E050_6508.xlsx for details (Hypotheses + Evidences)

+ The remaining LTIM liquid on the unit’s surface after test is vacuumed through the vacuum valve. The LTIM accumulates and flows through the gap between plunger and makes the plunger stuck; thus the plunger cannot move up to let the vacuum flowing from in to out => no vacuum.

+ The design of the CX1 AP does not have any sensors to detect the failed vacuum valve.

+ These 2 issues were escalated to TD but the solutions (replace better vacuum valve or add sensors) deem to have conflict with ROI (very high cost up to few millions USD vs. the unit reject quantity ~ 700 units so far). So this is considered CX1 AP design limitation and further options are still being explored but it will take longer time beyond this DRB due date.

 

 

# For residue VCTIM FM:

  1. Why didn’t PCS trigger the right cell A501?

problem_desc:
Executive Summary: 

MM#1

·       Currently; ADLS and RPLS products are facing a high failure rate on bent substrate (BS) issue at HDMx module. Based on data investigation; beside hardware wear and tear; 30% of BS was contributed by Sticky/TOS alarm. The root cause was defined to be unexpected behavior of AP pan de-actuation process after TOSCommandOperation alarm was raised. When the alarms TOSCommand Failure appeared; the AP will automatically disconnect and disengage without calling the de-actuation workflow leading to LTIM is not fully withdrawn. The consequence of the event is LTIM residue on unit surface which cause unit stick on pedestal then drop and OOP on the socket; BS will be happened after the robot arm pick the unit for the second test.

·       The improvement from skyline is that the de-actuation workflow is timely called when alarms occur to ensure no LTIM leftover as normal test sequence that can help unit not stuck in pedestal when AP disengage.

·       As alignment with QRE team; 2 products JSL and ADLS601 will be selected to cover for both lidded and bare die platform. After FWP is fully approved; the skyline workflow will be proliferated to all the products.

·       This learning was leveraged from RPLS8161 (WP approval#2023.16.AT Integrated CCB.143.FWP)

MM#2

·       From WW32.2D – WW33.1D: Data collection first 3 lots on 2 products ADLS601 and JSL at 2 tool HXV039 & HXV021 after released new skyline workflow.

• 5Why:
  1. Why did the ISL trigger for lot U330D614?
    • Because 26 units failed at REBI (6263)  although they had passed at Class Test (6262). There was a strong CA signal at 1 cell B401 at the HDMT tool. 
  2. Why did 26 units pass bin 1 at 6262 but fail bin 1905 at 6263?
    • Suspecting the Tray map issue happened at 6262 causing 1 VID to be linked with 2 different Efuse IDs.
  3. Why were impacted units induced by the Tray map issue at 6262 still moved out to 6263?
    • RFC guidance did not cover the Tray Map issue that happened at HDMT module then caused impacted units to escape to operation 6263.
  4. Why did the Tray map issue happen at Class Test 6262?
    • Because 02 untested trays were unintentionally swapped during processing at HDMT.LoadPort.B02.
  5. Why were 02 untested trays swapped at 6262?
    • There was a mismatch in the trays' position between PLC and Tool Controller (TC) during dispatching for 2 trays 0640 and 0639 from Stacker 2 to Eport at LP.B02.
  6. Why had a mismatch between PLC and TC for 2 trays 0640 and 0639?
  • Suspected two factors involved: 1) Tray movement was disrupted during transfer at the HDMT LoadPort with action of tray removal manually to fix OOP issue; 2) Software executed double tray movement commands instead of the expected single tray transit.
  • Some dispatches at LP.B were interrupted and did not complete/pause successfully while the LP.B door was opened to fix OOP units. These were combined factors that caused TC could not capture the correct position of trays 0640 and 0639 after the LP.B door was closed.

problem_desc:
Executive summary: From WW32'23; JSL product spike up significantly MI02 loss code with new sub app SI-DIE-T-STDK (mostly defect known as salt line staining). In the past; the defect's limit was relaxed; but currently; the product has transitioned from the ADVI tool to the DVI tool; so that limit inapplicable and leading to multiple triggered cases. As a consequence; there has been a rise in collateral down rate and an impact on the workload for EUPH/Operations. Additionally; there have been no abnormal findings in the HDMx hardware. All of these defects does not meet the rejection criteria; which has been identified as a known issue resulting from hardware limitations in the HDMx tool. Most of the cases exhibit the salt-line defect located at the two corners of the CPU/PCH die. The relaxation of the limit only applies to the candidate reject flag and does not affect units with a hard reject MI02. The PyPCS trigger incorporates another script to identify MI02H (>3u; utilizing IRVI data for running CA and triggering); resulting is low for escapee risk. Therefore; follow the 'PyPCS signal waiver process' and open a DRB#11657689 documentation to implement new PyPCS limit proposal.

problem_desc:
- On W47.4; at tool HXV028; cell#C401; TIU#RPLS816111T2677 down due PCS triggered bin 9985 (potential bent substrate issue); TRB HTX detected melted signature on Center Base during follow check list check TIU. On W47.5; we were informed that DVI server down and could not get data for lot running through this time frame then we routed lot X46K065 to BRTI and detected only 1 unit have dent signal but not reject due to not meet criteria; release lot to downstream. Until W48.1; DVI server was UTP and triggered this lot X246K065 had 5 unit dented (include 1 unit detected by BRTI) match with finding on TIU.  At this time; lot X246K065 already moved to IW. The 1st meeting was called to define impacted scope 1 lot with 377u and follow disposition we pulled back lot to demix 5 units impacted then measure Keyence. 

- On WW48.2; follow up meeting was called after having LYA result; data showed that all the units are low risk as they not meet the reject criteria however observed 2 units cracked on land pad then QRE decided to kill those units (for further study on actual risk assessment). All on-hold lot could be released. Initial investigation showed that there were four cases happens on difference TIUs; lot; tool-cell with the same pin location is D49 with leading hypothesis is shorted between VSS & VCCIN on pogo pin location caused the melted TIU socket.   As DVI-IA script is already re-enabled as containment action; it's highly confident that DVI-IA can detect the issue with low escapee risk; team is agreed to demote MRB to DRB. 

- After conducting multiple DOE to validate the hypothesis; the team was able replicate the issue and the root cause was confirmed that physical damaged unit (failed at EQA had short/crack signature) was run RV in different cells causing multiple TIU sockets melted. With the current process; RV units are checked by only naked eyes which has low capability to detect bad physical units. To minimize the risk of missing detect bad physical units during inspection; the team agreed to enhance the process to control the input (pre-HDMx) for RV units by using BRTI check both top and bottom sides of units. PE team will train the procedure for all CW and documents will be uploaded into the share drive for sustaining.

The TD team confirmed that fresh the VCTIM might induce FB1797 and burn base on historical burn happened in TD; and it doesn’t completely eliminate the issue. problem_desc:
Following the Preliminary White Paper (PWP) approved - Enable RetestExclusion Mode EWMA for Lunar Lake M442 (LNL M442) [Class III] which alignment to following start next phase Final White Paper (FWP) for all PPV Skyline products; PPV module following the strategy for enabling Retest Exclusion Mode “Exponentially Weighted Moving Average” EWMA for Alder Lake N (ADL N081).

PPV ADL N081 are running with RetestExclusion enabled and ExclusionMode='DisableAfterThreshold' which consider good cells (last tested unit is good) to perform testing a retested unit. We see an opportunity to improve how SW select cell for retesting with EWMA enable; EWMA considers the score based on list of units ran through cell. This behavior is supposed to improve how SW select good cells.

EWMA calculation:

- First unit: EWMA(0) = EWMASeed

- From second unit (n >= 0): EWMA(n+1) = (1- EWMALamda) * EWMA(n) + EWMALamda * result(n+1)

  • Summary of the proposed change:
  • Example: set Threshold='0.38' ~ 13.68 cells; below are comparison logic between ExclusionMode='DisableAfterThreshold' and ExclusionMode='EWMA'

     

    [*] EWMA disabled:

    <RetestExclusion ExclusionMode='DisableAfterThreshold' ResetMode='None' Threshold='0.38' EWMASeed='.1' EWMALambda='.1'/>

     

    1. When 1 unit finished testing on a cell; if 'PASS' then consider cell is 'GOOD'; otherwise cell is 'BAD'

    2. When 1 retest unit need to be processed; if # of 'BAD' cell exceeds threshold 0.38 ~ 13.68 cells then this unit can go to any available cell at that time; if not this unit will be excluded from 'BAD' cell list

     

    [**] EWMA enabled:

    <RetestExclusion ExclusionMode='EWMA' ResetMode='None' Threshold='0.38' EWMASeed='.1' EWMALambda='.1'/>

     

    1. When 1 unit finished testing on a cell; based on EWMA calculation; SW will generate EWMA score of each cell

    2. When 1 retest unit need to be processed; if # of 'BAD' cell exceeds threshold 0.38 ~ 13.68 cells then SW sorted EWMA score and only excluded from 3 worst cells (having highest score) at that time; if not this unit will be excluded from 'BAD' cell list

Event Summary: 

On 11/4/2025; an InTMS ticket flagged lot U543G920 (TWL) for high yield loss. The lot had been tested on 10/28/2025 at CLASS and moved out on 10/30/2025 at OLB. At the time of notification; approximately one thousand units had already been rejected due to the three-day restore limit in RIMS. Initial investigation found missing Unit Level Traceability (ULT) data uploaded at Class; leading to rejection at OLB. An offline detection script was created and immediately deployed.


On 11/5/2025; the offline detection script flagged lot U544B932 (ADLP6) for missing ULT data upload; showing the same symptom as lot U543G920. The lot was tested on 11/2/2025 at HXV043 (1A summary); then continued to test next summary (1B) and move out on 11/4/2025 at HXV014. The missing ULT data for summary 1A caused 567 units (Bin 1) to be rejected at OLB. These units were successfully withdrawn from RIMS and demixed for check-in to EIMS for reclaiming. Per the bonus-back checklist; this activity will be managed under the current DRB.


The confirmed root cause was the addition of a new attribute; naturalsspec; in the RC3.8 ULT chunk following an IPG request. This change prevented RC3.7 from parsing and uploading ULT data tested in RC3.8. Contributing factors included the removal of the DI check in TP at HDMx and a high yield loss threshold at OLB for all reject types.


As a corrective action; the CSR for detecting missing ULT data was enabled to automatically hold impacted lots before OLB. For prevention; a backward compatibility fix for ULT uploads between RC3.8 and RC3.7 was implemented in RC3.8 build 156+; which has been validated and is currently in data collection. However; the build does not yet have an FWP; so all software release progress for build 156+ will continue under a separate document: DRB#12500996.

Q1: Why need to qualify new firmware version 20.3.0.7

A1: This release addresses a number of bug and feature changes requested from ATM. The list of changes are…

 

- As a containment action for a larger module level network issue; the firmware process management was changed to ensure the TCC still services all tasks in times of network drops/congestion. When these larger module level network issues occur they can manifest in a number of ways including UEI related alarms; actuation issues and sometimes thermal bin97 failures. One note is these module network issues can manifest in a large number of ways; and this containment action specifically only looks to address where skyline (the host) and the AP/TCC (the client) are unable to communicate; and ensure the AP/TCC continues to perform what it was last instructed to do for up to 10 seconds. After 10 seconds the TCC will go into a lockout state for safety reasons around being unmanaged. This 10 second timeout is not new or changes with this FW release; just stating for the record.

 

- Implemented a containment action related to a MTL PPR sighting. It was found at times the test program would call for a delayed control set start; but immediately start sending additional control set changes.  The TP/PRIME team acknowledges this is a bug on their end but state they are not sure how to resolve this. With this in mind we will contain this in the FW by ensuring we follow the last control set change sent to the TCC. As PPR is not yet used in ATM; validation of this change will be a GRC effort in TD.

 

- Addressed a bug with the CX1-LFF pan specifically that prevented normal operation of the BLT EEPROMs. As this is a newer pan type and not yet used across ATM; validation will be a GRC effort in TD on GNR UCC.

 

- Added in two new multizone (MTZ) configurations requested for LunarLake. This new configurations will not be used for legacy products. As these new configurations are not planned to be used in ATM until early 2024; validation for this will be a GRC work in TD.

root_cause_desc:
Why#1: Why was units dent? Ans: because damaged AP pusher/plunger created dent mark on stiffener of units

Why#2: Why was AP pusher/plunger damaged? Ans: because it had been hit by PNB arm during Init step of Teaching flow?

Why#3: Why did PNB arm hit during Init step of Teaching flow? Ans: There is the high risk alarm (Y Gantry alarm) causing the SW can not detect the arm position and we don't have the effective response flow for high risk alarms (detail: during performing Z teach as trivial step of TIU teaching flow; Y-axis gantry movement got alarm and fail to move; user manually initialize the PNB. At that moment; with such coordinate of Y (-626.128); Software Logic will recognize that PNB gantry was in unsafe zone (potential to collide with AP) and would move Z-axis to Standby position before moving Y-axis home. The gantry moves up to expected safe travel z-height but failed to move in Y-axis. However; suddenly it had disconnection between Y-gantry motor with PLC controller; introduced a dummy value of Y axis coordinate (-1E10). This deceived value made Software thought that the PNB gantry were in safe zone to move; then it started to Z-home and Y-home; induced a crash on AP pusher frame.)

To fix or reduce this alarm; we propose to raise/increase the unit place/drop height in STHI handler recipe 2mm as picture below.

We document this proposal in this approved prelim white paper link https://xccb.intel.com/Documents/DocumentWorkspace.aspx?DocumentID=2274374.

root_cause_fix_summary: \\ Skyline patch validation
root_cause_desc:
W1: Why skip cold all units for impacted lots? 

A1: Because PdePlugin cannot find data of previous process step. 


W2: Why PdePlugin cannot find data of previous process step? 

A2: Because PdePluginPudlSubscriber did not received unit data of previous PS.  


W3: Why PdePluginPudlSubscriber did not received unit data of previous PS? 

A3: Because all DPC services disconnected then reconnected at ~20-30mins after midnight on impacted tools. 

The auto reconnect does not happen for PdePluginPudlSubscriber; 

TD provide the patch to address the DPC disconnection issue causing to missing PdePluginPudlSubscriber ( Bug 266501)


W4: Why all DPC services disconnected then reconnected at ~20-30mins after midnight on impacted tools? 

A4: Because the time on DPC drifted too far (15 secs) so all the ReliableSessions of DPC WCFs forced reconnect. Midnight is the time SkyZip starts running; and Windows Time-Service event 50 (time drifted >5s per 15mins) was logged ~2mins before disconnection. 


W5: Why was the time on DPC drifted too far at ~20-30mins after midnight on impacted tools? 

A5: Because SkyZip TimeSync sets DPC time to refer to TC time upon run. Both TC and DPC Time-Service are expected to sync with Domain Controller (default) so the time on these 2 PCs should be very closely matched. 

However; on all impacted tools; we detected that the TC (only) Windows Time-Service has Source='Free-running System Clock’. Thus; if the TC time drifts far enough from the DCs; issue will happen. 


W6: Why; on all impacted tools; the TC Windows Time-Service has Source='Free-running System Clock'? 

A6: Because the TC Windows Time-Service config is different from default: Type=NTP; Server=10.104.195.238 which is a DC that already been EOL by IT infra (mid Aug on papers; late Nov in reality - met with SC L2). 


W7: Why; on all impacted tools; the TC Windows Time-Service config is different from default? . 

A7: Unknow


W8: Why have the issue just happened recently?

A8: Server 10.104.198.238 which is a DC that already been EOL by IT infra mid Aug on papers. Then; it needs enough long time so that TC time drifted far enough from the DCs (late November)

  • Most of FCCSP/MBL/PCH product thermal recipe setup for chiller setpoint are different between hot (12*C) and cold (-35*C) operation.
  • From design standpoint; product running hot cold same operation thus chiller setpoint -35*C is the best solution for hardware while switching operation to avoid waiting time for chiller reaching new setpoint.
  • Most of CPU product hot and cold using -35*C which is observed high THA failure rate. In 2021; the project thermal recipe optimization (2022.02.AT Integrated CCB.96.PWP) apply for CPU (only on CMLS62/CMLS102); but with assumption low volume for other CPU product we didn’t leverage it.

problem_desc:
Problem Statement: ARLS816B has multiple cases stain on substrate due to LTIM spread out to subtrate top side and the defects are not meet reject criteria. Collaterals were down and checked without abnormal finding. After investigation; there is a finding on die force/total force during initial LTIM dispense (Stage 1 and stage 2); which is higher than technical recommendation. It could be causing spitting or splashing of LTIM. 

Die force/Total force at dispensing LTIM stage (stage 1 and stage 2 in STIM recipe) does not impact to final die force/total force applied on unit.
- Stage 1 and 2: Apply on unit for initial LTIM dispense; however the force of this stage does not fully touch on unit. It should be creating a gap between pedestal and die.
- Stage 3 and 4: This is final force; directly applied on unit to start testing. Do not change at this stage.

The DRB #is opened and begins data collection on ARLS816B under the approved PWP 2025.43.AT Integrated CCB.51.PWP.

Proposal: Reduce Die force and Total force at stage 1 and 2 to avoid LTIM splashing to substrate.

- Step1: Run 3 lots with NEW module recipe change; contain in DRB at back end.

- Step2: Review data based on QCs in PWP then release lot normally.

- Step 4: Revert back module recipe.

- Step3: Submit FWP + release new recipe revision.

On WW23.1D; RTI detected lot ADLN U522F878-7820 has units stain on die; then rework to defmet for checking stain on substrate bottom side. Result that defmet detected this lot has a total of 65 units with stains on the substrate ball side (39 units meet the criteria; 26 units do not meet the criteria). Some cells had a high failure rate at HXV005. Following the RFC; due to the total impact being greater than 20 units; a meeting was called with stakeholders to define the risk assessment; containment scope; and disposition plan. In the meeting discussions; for defects in lot U522F878; it was determined to be LOW RISK; then follow LCAD/open SYI for 65 units with stains on the substrate ball side (39 units meet the criteria; 26 units do not meet the criteria). Furthermore; the module needs to update more investigation for lot X522L709 triggered by FVI-7333 (due to CA at cell A202; A501 – which has not been discussed in the periodic meeting).

 

As a result of the pending AR of the 1st management; further analysis shows N-4 to N-8 and last lot in tool have similar stain signals on the bottom side that meet the reject criteria of LCAD. With this finding; the current hypothesis is that the stain occurs across 13 cells on HXV005. The meeting has been called to discuss the impacted scope and containment; and the team agreed to contain an additional 13 child lots compared to the previous meeting (10 lots in IW ~ around 12ku and 3 lots in WIP). The 3 lots in WIP have been reworked to FVI with clean results; and 10 lots are to be processed and pulled back.

#Per review DVI E-app image for whole lot tested at HXV005; we defined the start point is lot run at HXV005 at 30/5/2025 ( 1st lot impacted is U522F266); total 10 lot U impacted after 30/5/2025 with total 24 unit flag heavy stain at bottom side; the stain intermittently happens on lot.


#Detailing the total of 24 units: 3 units have already undergone FVI and are clean (the DVI E-app image captured the stain as well). 5 units are currently on hold in WIP; and the remaining 16 units have reached IW with stains. Out of these; 2 units have heavy stains compared to the units captured by the DVI E-app but are clean after FVI; while the remaining 14 units have stains comparable to those seen in the FVI.

QRE suggests pulling back a total of 16 units (from 10 lot X) from IW to scan with FVI to determine whether they meet the rejection criteria or not.

TSP AP Cold Plate (part to allow the coolant fluid going through the thermal head) degraded after long time running in production and led to EGDI leaks out. EGDI leaks to socket and causing stain on unit.

root_cause_desc:
1. Why do we need to run this DOE TCU 02-step actuation?

- Because PIYL is gating TFC for ADL P682 at PPV contributing to 0.04% MI02 Yield Loss higher than goal 0.025%.

2. Why ADL P682 is having high MI02 Yield loss?

- Because most of the case have finding strong CA at PPV with failure mode is VCTIM shifted at bin 1 corner + LTIM dispose causing high MI02 stain on die.
problem_desc:
In Q1’22; ADL-P682 has been starting massive ramp at STHI and it is detected VCTIM shift failure which has been inducing high yield loss in VNAT; loss code MI02 (stain on die). The failure mode is VCTIM shifting at bin 1 corner during processing and cycling unit; it happened ~ 80% occurrences out of all cases at STHI. One of mitigation action is to apply TCU 2-step actuation (recommended by TD) which expects to help reduce contact force between TCU pedestal (surface covered by VCTIM) and top side of unit (die surface with ADL-P682) while current TCU actuation logic is 1-step actuation. Initial DOE by Eng TP (intercept TCU 2-step actuation) with certain cells at VNAT showed positive result; it was shared to TD/IDC by ww11’22. Recommendation is to pilot at Prod tool to get more conclusive data. Refer attachment for detail.


Purpose: New TCU 02-step actuation method to mitigate VCTIM shifted issue and reduce the MI02 yield loss.

problem_desc:
TGLU42\ADLP282\ADLP682 products now have a high PyPCS trigger MI02 loss code that has high impact on EUPH/Operation workload; with sub-app SI-DIE-T-STDK/ SI-DIE-T-FM as the primary trigger. According to historical data; PyPCS was activated using the sub-app SI-DIE-T-STDK on TGLU42/ADLP682 and SI-DIE-T-FM on ADLP282 to detect the Black stain MI02 signal; but the faults did not meet the IRVI reject requirements. More than 75% of cases in TGLU42 and ~90% in ADL-P have salt line in the four corners of the CPU/PCH dies. All cases have no abnormal findings on HDMx hardware which was considered as a limitation of the handler side. After reviewing with ADVI ME/HDMx ME/ QRE across VF; they confirmed that these signals were over triggers and cannot optimize by module recipe as it might cause other defects to escape. Additionally; PyPCS implementation uses IRVI data for running CA; which handles both reject and hard reject candidates; so the risk for escapee is low.

 

  • WW39.1D; The team decided to relax the limit on a specific sub-app SI-DIE-T-STDK for the TGLU42 product to eliminate invalid triggers and improve EUPH/Operation burden under DRB#11247606 while expecting the revised logic of the PyPCS script; which is currently being coded and validated.

DTS trim isn't effective in catching DTS failures at LTTC when there's a clear shifted in the DTS slope fuse token. To tackle this; a method was created to catch this situation. Both QRE and TE agree to turn on the OFFLINE_HDMX_DTS Slope Check per Socket script to handle this. After enabling this script; there was total 6 cases trigger as below. Based on data collection; 6 cases trigger at VNAT consider invalid following the suggestion RFC from QRE. The team proposes to close with PSA DRB for documentation and proceed with further discussion with RFC execution practice.

 

1st trigger:

                On W20.3D; an abnormality was detected in the measurement value triggered by RPLP682 OFFLINE_HDMX_DTS_slope_Check_per_Socket script with the commonality hardware at CLASS. On W20.4D; a meeting was called to assess the risk and develop a plan for disposition. DRB#11529502 was initiated for data collection.

root_cause_desc:
Cause Analysis : At the impacted cell; before the issue happened; the tester triggered a TOS (Tester Operation System) alarm; causing a trip due to a TIER II alarm (safety alarm). As a consequence; the actuation pan de-actuated while the unit had not completed the LTIM (Liquid Thermal Interface Material) withdrawal; causing the unit to stick on the actuation pan and drop. Once the unit dropped; it became offset and was not properly aligned with the socket. As the arm attempted to move into the socket to pick it out; the unit was misaligned; causing it to scrape against the socket when the arm tried to retry picking it three times; resulting in the capacitor on the bottom side of the unit falling into the socket. The TOS alarm causing unit stickiness/out of pocket off-set and potential capacitor drop (when the arm tries to pick it out) is a known issue at HDMX (High-Density Modular Test). Therefore; we have created the RFC (Response follow checklist) to prevent this in case unit out of pocket happens. Then; the socket will be checked to confirm it does not cause further unit impact due to the dent substrate issue as a consequence of the unit being sticky/OOP and the previous capacitor drop. But the RFC currently mentions RPL8161 products; and in this case; the impacted product is RPR8161. As a result; the operator was not aware and did not follow the RFC requirements; which include opening the door to check the unit physically when the Tester TOS alarm is triggered.

Excursion summary:

- On January 22nd 2026; after processed 2 lots LNLM442 X552L536/ X602J535 at Lazer Mark module TMX-7300; tool triggered total 39 units mismatch quantity between ULT and Mars database. Initial investigation showed that these impacted units came from 1 abnormal tray when uploading data at HDMx module; lot X602J414-6197-HXV009; made missing OLF_SSPEC value from ULTRA database. As ULT mismatch will make data integrity concern; so DRB #12538076 was initiated to re-upload OLF_SSPEC in ULT DB then rework FVI to compare marking between 39 units mismatch ULT and good units to check any difference/abnormality. Total containment is 2 impacted lots in WIP with 3.3ku. Module Automation Engineer (MAE) team will schedule a follow-up meeting to define the root cause and Corrective Action/Preventive Action for this issue.

 

MM - Lump in meeting:


- On January 30th 2026; CSR trigger on-hold lot X604G606_6197 with failure mode ULT mismatch for 909 units at FUSE - 6197. Initial investigation showed that there have 20 chunks that cannot upload to NetApp; after repair lot 909 successfully upload to NetApp matching with trigger. As ULT mismatch will make data integrity concern and root cause is the same with DRB #12538076; so lot X604G606_6197 lump-in to DRB #12538076 with rework from 6511 to 6197/main route for rescreen Edispose. MM - Closure meeting:


- On February 5th 2026; all impacted lots were completed to run EQA with no abnormality in data upload and had been released. After conducting a deep-dive investigation from SC L2 & ULT L2 & MSD team; we identified the root cause and defined follow-up actions to prevent recurrence.

  • Main rootcause: The mismatch between network speed of Switch (1GB/Full duplex) and Tool's PC (Auto Negotiation) caused the network connection was disrupt intermittent.
  • Escapee rootcause:
    • Lot X552L536 & X602J535 escaped to Laser mark (operation 7300): The current RFC of CSR ULT mismatch did not mention that we need to check OLF_SSPEC value after recovering ULT data at HDMx for lots already moved in OLB module.

- MAE team will work with MSD to re-config the network speed of Switches to ensure they are matching with setting on tool's PCs (Auto Negotiation). MAE team also worked with SC L2 to revise the current RFC to be more robust to be able to cover corner scenarios like this issue.

problem_desc:
From QS (w19'2024) to HVM (w19'2025); LNL M442 product has started encountering issues associated with VCCATOM area. The issues occurred due to the melting of LTS balls at the VCCATOM area of the unit after testing at PPV; leading to several problems:
 - Yield loss: The VCCATOM failure results in failure bins 7104; 7105; 7130; 7506; and 7540; which induces to both 1A yield and final yield.
 - Elastomer Socket life cycle degradation: The LTS ball remains on the Elastomer Socket and cannot be removed; which contributes to the failure bins above. To maintain product performance; replacing the contaminated elastomer is essential. The socket's lifecycle has been degraded compared to the expected lifespan of 25;000 cycles and also impact to the cost due to replacing new Elastomer Socket.
 - Unit cosmetic: The LTS ball shape of unit at the VCCATOM area is melted and deformed.
 Engineering data showed that increasing the Die Force from 65lbs to 85lbs helps improve the overall contact between the unit and the Elastomer Socket. Thus; reducing the issue of LTS ball melted and potentially improve yield.

  • Base on MCC assessment; TF/DF 100/85 is acceptable.

root_cause_desc:
1. Why do we need to enable this RetestExclusion Mode EWMA on LNL?

  • This RetestExclusion Mode EWMA supposes to improve yield/2A recovery rate 

2. Why this change can improve yield/2A recovery rate?

  • We see an opportunity to improve how SW select better cells for retesting with EWMA enable

3. Why EWMA enable can improve how SW select cell for retesting?

  • EWMA calculate EWMA score based on the result of list unit ran through cell to select list cell to disable for retesting; compare to EWMA disable which only based on previous result on cell
problem_desc:
As of now; most of HVM products are running with RetestExclusion enabled and ExclusionMode='DisableAfterThreshold' which consider good cells (last tested unit is good) to perform testing a retested unit. We see an opportunity to improve how SW select cell for retesting with EWMA enable; EWMA considers the score based on list of units ran through cell. This behavior is supposed to improve how SW select good cells.
EWMA calculation:
- First unit: EWMA(0) = EWMASeed
- From second unit (n >= 0): EWMA(n+1) = (1- EWMALamda) * EWMA(n) + EWMALamda * result(n+1)

  • Summary of the proposed change:


Example: set Threshold='0.083' ~ 3 cells; below are comparison logic between ExclusionMode='DisableAfterThreshold' and ExclusionMode='EWMA'

[*] EWMA disabled:
<RetestExclusion ExclusionMode='DisableAfterThreshold' ResetMode='None' Threshold='0.083' EWMASeed='.1' EWMALambda='.1'/>
1. When 1 unit finished testing on a cell; if 'PASS' then consider cell is 'GOOD'; otherwise cell is 'BAD'
2. When 1 retest unit need to be processed; if # of 'BAD' cell exceeds threshold 0.083 ~ 3 cells then this unit can go to any available cell at that time; if not this unit will be excluded from 'BAD' cell list

[**] EWMA enabled:
<RetestExclusion ExclusionMode='EWMA' ResetMode='None' Threshold='0.083' EWMASeed='.1' EWMALambda='.1'/>
1. When 1 unit finished testing on a cell; based on EWMA calculation; SW will generate EWMA score of each cell
2. When 1 retest unit need to be processed; if # of 'BAD' cell exceeds threshold 0.083 ~ 3 cells then SW sorted EWMA score and only excluded from 3 worst cells (having highest score) at that time; if not this unit will be excluded from 'BAD' cell list

root_cause_fix_summary: DRB is opened to document for shipping material prior FWP approved. No CA/PA needed
root_cause_desc:
• Leading hypothesis: DPC SW components not using available memory efficiently; therefore tools running high complexity products at high volume are at risk of DPC SW crash with OutOfMemory error (worst time-between-failure seen is 14days on HXV030) 

 

For tools running complex products (LNL; MTL; ARL) at high volume; DPC memory will accumulate: 

  • MongoDB service increase at ~4.4GB/day until hit maximum ~54GB (~50% RAM) in ~12days (blue in example chart below) 
  • dpc.engine service swings drastically from baseline (15-25GB) to maximum available memory (red in example chart below)

Afterwards; DPC will continuously run at high DPC memory usage condition 


This DOE extends the pagefile to give the DPC more virtual memory to use. 

For example: on 1 tool the windows recommended size is 17267 

 

We chose the DOE number as 30000 to give +50% buffer to the ~20000 recommended size. As pagefile is hard disk space used as memory; it is slower than RAM memory; therefore increasing it too much might cause other slowness in the DPC.
problem_desc:
From mid Q4’24 till EoQ1’25; there were 13 SPOF events on multiple HDMx tools in VNAT because of DPC mongo crashed with error OutOfMemory. Observing ~62% events (8/13) happened on product LNL. While the rate of 6 SPOFs / quarter / whole fleet is not the top pareto for SW SPOF; it was a contributing factor into a missed shipment of LNL on 25’W09.

After consulting TD partners (ticket Bug 300867); we’ll perform DOE to extend the pagefile on DPC PC from the current setting (6000-10000 in 5M+E) to 30000-60000 to allow more memory for DPC SW components to use that might mitigate SPOF events. In 2020; there was a similar effort to extend pagefile for TA PC (2020.43.AT Integrated CCB .130.FWP) to mitigate TA SW crash issue. 

DOE parameters: 

  • Tool: HXV030 (LNL non-DRAM 6248) 
  • Timeframe: 2025 W14.2 – W17.2 (because the problem is accumulation of DPC memory usage after at least ~2weeks of full WIP) 

We shall submit ClassIV FWP to update the HDMx DPC pagefile; with the data collection plan: 3 samples 

  • 10ku before apply change (W14.1 – 14.2D) 
  • 10ku after apply change (W14.2N – 14.3D) à This DRB is opened to contain and review data for this sample to confirm no impact to baseline 
  • 10ku at peak DPC memory usage (W16.2D-N; ~12days after change; assuming full WIP)

5 Why:

Q1: Why does this issue occur?
A1: The VCTIM is damaged; exposing the TIM; which stains the unit's die during Thermal Head actuation.
 

Q2: Why is the VCTIM damaged?
A2: The conditioning process involves long heating times (85°C for 100 minutes) and constant interaction with mechanical units; making the VCTIM easier to damage during production.


Q3: Why is there a long heating time in the conditioning process?
A3: The heating time is determined by dwell time settings; currently set at 30 seconds for both up (de-actuation) and down (actuation) phases; with the up phase being unnecessarily long.


Q4: Why are both dwell times set at 30 seconds?
A4: The current firmware only allows input one number for both dwell times (hard config)
->Installing new firmware will allow separate dwell time settings; reducing heating time (by reducing dwell time up) and minimizing VCTIM damage.


  • Occurred root cause: Current VCTIM replacement process (long heating time) leading to the TIM exposed after undergoing many cycles. This TIM directly contacted the die of the unit; resulting in stain transfer.

problem_desc:
Currently; there have been multiple cases of the MI04/MI05 loss code being triggered on ADLS601/ADLS881/RPLS601/RPLS881 product by PyPCS. This has led to an increase in the collateral down rate and has had an impact on the workload for EUPH/Operations. This failure mode occurred across TIUs; but no abnormal findings were found in the HDMx hardware.  

Upon investigation; it was found that:

      + For MI04: PYPCS triggered under sub-app COMPONENT_3D_OR_PASSIVE_2D; all triggers were invalid for HDMx. Most of the cases were flagged at multiple capacitors; but no abnormal findings were found in the defect box and no units rejected after running thru IRVI and HW no findings also. The issue was suspected that's over trigger from DVI tool

      + For MI05: PYPCS triggered under sub-app CSI-XGA-B-ST; all triggers were invalid for HDMx. Most of the cases were flagged at bottom side of unit; but all the cases were no abnormal findings for TIU (still have stain mark on unit but this failure mode not come from HDMX) and no units rejected after running thru IRVI. The issue was suspected incoming and not related to TIU of HDMX


So the team intends to temporarily exclude the sub-app COMPONENT_3D_OR_PASSIVE_2D and CSI-XGA-B-ST for PYPCS candidate rule (still keep PYPCS hard reject rule for MI04/MI05 )in order to reduce the rate of invalid triggers and improve the workload for EUPH/Operations in alignment with QRE.  

Team will follow the 'PyPCS signal waiver process' to open a DRB# for data collection and go with FWP for permanent change once have enough data


The trigger rate significantly reduces after releasing the new limit and the MI05 hard reject units still flag and trigger the MI05H PYPCS rule as normal (to ensure no escapees for MI05 at the HDMX module). Therefore; we have aligned with QRE that close this DRB and submit the FWP later for permanent change for MI05 candidate reject for ADLS/RPLS products

·         Because EHL/EHB PPV motherboard could not bleed under power-off threshold

problem_desc:
Background: 
In VNAT PPV; EHL and EHB product observed high occurrence of Standby cell type 2 which is top 1 cell availability impact; up to 8% of weekly PTIU. When break down by alarm; ~70% total impact time induced by marginal Motherboards unable to shutdown properly.
While failure happen; observed that rail 12V_DCIN power rail on motherboard; which used for MB power-off check remained above the threshold of 0.8V.
The existing resistor value of 100k on location R3F15 is not strong enough to pull the 12V_DCIN power to completely bleed off while shutting down MB.
Proposed to reduce the resistor value from 100k to 10k to strongly pull the 12V power to ground and ensure the voltage is completely bleed off.
Offline data showed RSMRST resistor at location R3F15 rework able to help reduce failure.

Executive summary: 

On ww34.6N; Def-met team triggered lot RPL8161_U233G788 had 1370u got stain on lid signal (FI26). Base on FVI report; there were 1325u not meeting reject and 102u meeting reject criteria. This was 1st lot running through HXV019 after 5 days idling and there was no CA; the issue happened across cells at HXV019. In the same day; there was another event triggered same signal at HXV040 (lot #U233H180) with 97u having same symptom (FI26 not meet reject criteria); there was no CA at cells as well. The leading hypothesis is suspected as tool idling long time combining with contaminated pedestal surface causing stain on lid. In order to stop bleeding the issues; all AP pedestals were cleaned at 3 tools by ww35.4N. Some rejected units and pedestals were sent to LYA to understand contaminated materials and support stain Task Force. Due to recent FACR concern for units not meeting reject criteria; QRE/CQE recommended to not ship these marginal units to End-user market. Total 52ku (35ku in WIP and 17ku in warehouse) were contained under this MRB and routed to FVI for rescreening and segregating 3ku marginal units following LCAD spec with threshold 50u/lot. Additionally; FVI was enabled 100% after Class Test in order to monitor the effectiveness of pedestal cleaning action and support engineering team on improvement plan in next 2 weeks. There is no backlog impact in ww36 (no backlog in ww35) and no shipment risk in ww35.

Closure meeting: Scanning all lidded products; the issue stain grid patterns on lid not only happens on RPLS8161 but also happens across product platform including server and desktop; across VF sites. Issue was escalated and FT was formed involving TD and VF Engs for solution. After long investigation; the primary root cause is due to technology design: Interaction between AP pedestal surface and lid surface with LTIM chemical reaction under test condition (test time; thermal; power). The interaction causes stain grid pattern on the lid surface of unit while tool or cells idling is contribution factor which makes units more severe. The xRB team agreed to close the DRB without PA while several CAs were already implemented; engineer team will keep monitoring to ensure Yield loss and RCR rate hit the goal. Furthermore; for RPLS816 splitting units do not meet reject criteria is no longer require; QRE agreed to stop this activity; Test team will call a meeting with relevant stakeholders to pass down the change. Besides; all the processes; routes and RFC are backed to POR. For NPI products if facing same issue during NPI; ME will call separate discussion with QRE; open xRB if needed for next steps.

problem_desc:
The TIU XIU Check has been identified as the top trigger pareto for ADL N/ADL PS/MTL product. The root cause of this issue is attributed to a misalignment between the PC and TIU BB; induced by a recent change in the alignment hole on the PC. This misalignment is observable both immediately after assembling the TIU in the TRB and during subsequent testing in the production cell. The impact of this misalignment is reflected in the higher triggers on downrate. To address this issue and improve the alignment; we propose changing the screw used on the Top TIU PC Stiffener. Currently; the screw only secures the PC to the BB through the Stiffener; but the new design proposal aims to enhance the screw's function. The modified screw will keep the PC securely fixed in the correct location; preventing any movement during operation in the production cell or assembly in the TRB. This adjustment is expected to enhance the alignment of the pin in BOB to the pad on the PC; ultimately reducing XIU failures. PWP# 2023.46.AT Integrated CCB.55.PWP approved to collect the data on ADL N product. The lot run thru DOE TIU will be on hold at backend to review the Yield performance properly.
